transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am afraid that my duty as Kapellmeister is to serve the Imperial House, and to promote its musical interests. I cannot allow composers whose works do not align with the standards and traditions of the Court to receive appointments. It is important to maintain the highest level of musical excellence and to uphold the reputation of the Court. I am willing to discuss this matter with you, Your Majesty, but I cannot compromise on my principles.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your principles, Salieri, are indeed admirable when they serve the Empire. But when they serve only *your* interests, or when they selectively apply to certain talents while others are denied, then they become rather less so. "Standards and traditions," you say. Are you suggesting that innovation, or a different style, automatically falls short of these "standards"? Are we to hear only what *you* deem acceptable? And these "rival composers" — are they truly lacking, or merely different? I ask again, Salieri: Explain yourself. These letters suggest a pattern, not an isolated incident of upholding quality.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your Majesty, I understand your concerns and I assure you that my intentions have always been to prioritize the musical well-being of the Imperial House. However, I must admit that there have been instances where I have held back certain composers due to their musical style or lack thereof. I believe that maintaining a consistent level of excellence in the arts is crucial for the image and reputation of the Court. It is true that innovation and diversity are essential aspects of the musical world, but it is also important to ensure that the works produced are of a high quality and align with the values and traditions of the Empire. I apologize if my actions have caused any inconvenience or dissatisfaction, but I hope you can understand my reasoning behind them.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Lack thereof," Salieri? That is a most peculiar phrase to use when speaking of a composer's work. Does a composer simply *lack* a style, or does their style simply not appeal to *your* ear? And as for "values and traditions of the Empire"—since when has musical style been so intrinsically linked to the moral fiber of the Holy Roman Empire? Are we to believe that a fugue is more virtuous than a sonata, or that a particular orchestration offends the very principles of our House?

You speak of inconvenience and dissatisfaction, but these letters speak of careers stifled, of talent overlooked, of unfair advantage taken. These are not minor grievances, but serious accusations of a misuse of your considerable influence. Tell me, which composers have you found so utterly lacking in "style" as to warrant such suppression? Give me names, Salieri, and tell me precisely how their *music* failed to align with the "values and traditions" of this court. I require specifics, not veiled generalities.
